currentRankImpact.interpretation: Current snapshot illustration only. Same production graph, reference population, scored games and outcomes. Better outcome-link scores alone do not prove a fairer SOR order.

status: Offline retrospective research; FCS SOR stays Experimental. No production promotion.
limitations: All evaluation seasons were previously inspected. This split prevents new fitting on the evaluation outcomes, but is not an untouched historical holdout. Seasons 2021-2022 influenced the original Strength engine selection. Corrected retrospective source data are not proof of historical as-published availability.

A better per-game probability link does not establish a uniquely correct or fairer SOR achievement ordering. Keep FCS SOR Experimental; assess sensitivity, reference probabilities, subdivision coverage and rank changes separately.

The transferred FBS baseline was originally fitted on 2014-2019, including 226 direct FBS-FCS selection targets in 2018-2019 and indirect FCS-FCS graph context. New FCS candidates use only 2014-2017 before selection. The unequal baseline exposure means retention is conservative, not independent proof the baseline is superior.
Final-network leave-one-game-out features include other later results; they are descriptive reconstructions, never pregame forecasts.
Source season labels and incomplete FCS/lower-division schedules remain coverage limits. Independent feature reproduction does not certify every historical input.
Cross-division venues are highly selected. Coefficients are not a causal estimate of a neutral-field subdivision talent gap.
Twenty-twenty is a tiny partial spring/fall source stress slice, not a full FCS season.
